items.correct: In the mouth — mechanically by teeth and chemically by amylase in saliva.
items.why: Digestion starts in the mouth; the stomach and small intestine continue it.

items.q: How do digestive enzymes break down food?
items.correct: Chemically, splitting large molecules into small soluble ones.
items.misconception: Physically, by cutting food like tiny teeth.
items.random_wrong: By absorbing the food into the blood.
items.why: Teeth do the physical breakdown; enzymes chemically break large molecules (e.g. starch → glucose).

items.correct: No — they are needed in tiny amounts for health, not for energy.
items.misconception: Yes, vitamins are a main energy source.
items.random_wrong: Vitamins are only found in meat.
items.why: Energy comes from carbohydrates and fats; vitamins support processes like vision and immunity.

items.q: Is all dietary fat bad for you?
items.correct: No — some fat is essential; excess saturated fat is the health risk.
items.misconception: Yes, all fat should be avoided completely.
items.why: Fat stores energy, insulates and forms membranes; the issue is too much, especially saturated fat.
